Sports.title: Unai Emery criticises his own Aston Villa players as Spaniard hits out at side's lack of discipline in search of first Premier League win of the season
Sports.content:
Unai Emery criticises his own Aston Villa players as Spaniard hits out at side's lack of discipline in search of first Premier League win of the season

Unai Emery has criticised some of his Aston Villa players for lacking discipline as they seek their first league win of the season.

Villa had Joao Gomes sent off on his debut on the opening day of the campaign when they lost 4-0 at Brighton, and Emery took off Nicolas Jackson at half-time of last weekend's home defeat by Nottingham Forest as he feared the forward would receive a second yellow card.

Villa have had seven other bookings in their first four Premier League fixtures, as well as three in the Champions League win over Club Brugge, and three more in the Carabao Cup victory at Coventry.

Emery said: 'We must control our emotions, individually. We must reduce red cards but also some yellow cards are not necessary.

'Aaron Wan-Bissaka's yellow card at Coventry (for squaring up to Gustavo Hamer) was not normal. He and Jackson are experienced players and they must control it.

'We've spoken about it in the dressing room. It's very important in terms of how we want to build our mentality. We need to focus on playing.'

Unai Emery has taken aim at his Aston Villa players for their lack of discipline in the opening weeks of the season

Part of the reason former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca lost patience with Jackson was the forward's habit of picking up yellow cards.

Jackson has yet to score in the Premier League for Villa since moving from Stamford Bridge for £65million in the summer.

Sports.title: Olympic star Keely Hodgkinson reveals bizarre 'abnormality' after MRI discovery following latest injury scare: 'My body is built differently'
Sports.content:
Olympic star Keely Hodgkinson reveals bizarre 'abnormality' after MRI discovery following latest injury scare: 'My body is built differently'

Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson says an MRI scan has revealed she has an 'abnormality' in her hamstring.

After a suspected tear last year, Hodgkinson discovered she had a 'split' hamstring, giving her two tendons instead of one.

The 24-year-old has continued running despite learning of the anomaly, although she is still trying to determine whether it is a blessing or a curse.

Following her second-place finish behind Switzerland's Audrey Werro in the 800m final at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest earlier this month, Hodgkinson announced she had sustained another hamstring tear at the European Championships in Birmingham a few weeks earlier.

Hodgkinson said: 'My body is quite literally built different. I have two tendons where the tendon tore (last year). So where everyone has one tendon, mine is split, so I have two.

'We’re trying to figure out if it’s a strength or a weakness. So when one of them tore, I still had the other one because it split like this. You don’t feel the injury until later on, when it got a bit tight.'

After a suspected tear last year, Hodgkinson discovered she had a 'split' hamstring, giving her two tendons instead of one

Hodgkinson believes it is something she was born with, adding: 'It’s just how I’m made. We found out last year when I tore it on the MRI scan.

'As a pro, it means that when one is down, I can still run on the other one that works. But as a con, maybe it’s slightly weaker than the other one that’s attached.'

Hodgkinson's primary concern, particularly after two injury-plagued years, including a lay-off lasting more than 12 months, was how it would affect her racing.

'It’s a weird one,' Hodgkinson explained. 'You can still run on them, there’s no danger of it moving (to the other one).

'I haven’t missed any training over the last three weeks. I’ve just had to alter my approach, take my foot off the speed because that’s when it’s most risky, and go at it from a strength perspective. My body heals very, very well, so I couldn’t really feel anything.

'It feels good. I’ve not really felt anything for, like, two weeks now. It’s more the mental side. You’re very hyper-aware, like, "Oh, is that something? Is it not? Do I trust my body to go again?".'

Since claiming Olympic gold in Paris in 2024, Hodgkinson's progress has been repeatedly disrupted by injury. A hamstring problem suffered the following February sidelined her for more than a year before she finally returned to competition.

She made an immediate impact on her comeback in August 2025, winning successive Diamond League races, before carrying that momentum into the following indoor season. Hodgkinson broke the world indoor 800m record in February and added World Indoor gold a month later.

Her outdoor campaign, however, has proved more challenging. The Briton has been beaten three times by Werro this year, including in the race where she surrendered her European title to the Swiss athlete.

Hodgkinson concludes her season on Friday night in London at Athlos, the all-female competition launched by Reddit founder Alexis Ohanian

Hodgkinson recently revealed that a fall while jogging along a Manchester canal during a warm-down left her with cuts to both knees and a jarring impact to her back, an incident she described as turning recent months into a 'battle'.

While she acknowledged the accident may have played a part in the hamstring issue that forced her to miss Diamond League meetings in Zurich and Brussels, Hodgkinson insisted she was not using it as an excuse for her performances.

'Part of me wants to talk about it and then part of me doesn't, because I feel like my words get twisted or people are like "oh, she's making excuses",' Hodgkinson said.

'Going into the Europeans, I thought I was in the best shape ever. But when I fell over, that kind of messed me up way more than I thought it did. I think that's what contributed to my hamstring, because I couldn't really use my quad for a while.'

Hodgkinson concludes her season on Friday night in London at Athlos, the all-female competition launched by Reddit founder Alexis Ohanian.

Sports.title: I saw a different side to Michael Carrick after Man United's loss to Brighton - and here's why alarm bells should be ringing for United fans, writes CHRIS WHEELER
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's experience of the Old Trafford circus was one of the reasons Manchester United brought him back to the club as head coach in January, and he has put it to good use ever since.

Triumph and adversity have been met with an easy smile and well-chosen comment from a man who, by and large, has seen it all in a United career that began two decades ago. For Carrick, blocking out the external noise is second nature.

But in the wake of a disastrous Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton on Wednesday night, we saw a different side to the 45-year-old. Carrick looked agitated – emotional even – after United were beaten at Old Trafford for the second time in four days.

It wasn’t on the same scale as his predecessor Ruben Amorim’s meltdown when United went out of this competition at Grimsby last season, sitting drenched in the dugout, fiddling with his tactics tray and incapable of watching his team lose on penalties.

Nor was it another flash of anger like the one that led to Carrick snapping at interviewer Jan Aage Fjortoft for his ‘ridiculous’ question about United’s lack of passion in the opening-day defeat at Hull.

But for a man who knows the lie of the land at Old Trafford so well, Carrick seemed genuinely shocked by how quickly this season is unravelling – and how fast he must now put it right – following three defeats in six games from a relatively gentle start.

Michael Carrick looked agitated, shocked – emotional even – after his Manchester United side were beaten at Old Trafford for the second time in four days

United defender Ayden Heaven can't bear to look as United slump to a 3-2 defeat on Wednesday night

Since Everton stunned United with a stoppage-time equaliser 11 days ago, his team have lost the Manchester derby and gone out of the cup to Brighton, either side of a Champions League stroll against Sabah of Azerbaijan.

Even the storm surrounding JJ Gabriel’s decision to quit United barely warranted a mention late on Wednesday night as Carrick faced the TV cameras and written press with the boos of United fans still ringing in his ears.

‘A couple of smallish things end up accumulating and, let’s be honest, it feels bigger. All of a sudden it becomes a greater thing from nowhere,’ he admitted.

‘It’s happened over a period of maybe two or three weeks where there’s a lot of frustration and disappointment around, and we need to flip that and start winning games again.

‘Being here toughens you up. It’s all about what you do next and dealing with the ups and the downs.’

We have seen plenty of managers wilt in the pressure cooker of Manchester United in the 13 years since Sir Alex Ferguson stepped down, among them some hugely experienced coaches like Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes and Ralf Rangnick.

The comparison United would most like to avoid with Carrick, of course, is Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

There is no certainty at all that Carrick’s spell in charge will follow the same path as his old friend and team-mate, but the parallels are unavoidable.

Two ex-United favourites with limited experience of coaching at the highest level who were parachuted into one of the biggest clubs in the world as interim manager and did well enough to earn the job on a full-time basis.

There is no certainty at all that Carrick’s spell in charge will follow the same path as his old friend and team-mate Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, but the parallels are unavoidable

Even the storm surrounding JJ Gabriel’s decision to quit United barely warranted a mention as Carrick faced the Press with the boos of United fans still ringing in his ears

History has been a little unkind to Solskjaer. Yes, he lost six of his next 10 games after signing a three-year contract in March 2019 with Carrick on his first-team staff.

But Solskjaer lasted another two-and-a-half seasons, finishing second and third in the Premier League, and was within a penalty shootout of winning the Europa League.

It’s a record that looks better in retrospect, but the view remains that the decision to hand him the job permanently was the wrong one.

When United sought a quick replacement for Amorim in January, Solskjaer and Carrick were available and immediately pushed to the top of the pile of candidates because director of football Jason Wilcox placed great importance on their ability to fit straight into a unique environment they both know so well.

Ultimately, Solskjaer lost out because it felt like too much of a backward step to United and there was some concern over the lack of discretion coming from his camp during the negotiations.

Carrick was seen as the more progressive choice and it was rewarded with a run of just two defeats in 17 games and Champions League qualification.

In April, a month before he was handed a two-year contract, he dismissed the comparisons with Solskjaer, saying: ‘It’s irrelevant really, it really is. That’s not a negative or a positive, it doesn’t really have any link at all.

‘It’s a different time and a different team now, irrespective of me or who's in charge, so I don't really think comparisons make any difference.’

Even at this early stage of the season, though, the poor start is reminiscent of the dip after Solskjaer’s permanent appointment amid concerns that United have left Carrick without the tools to compete with his rivals in the Premier League and Europe.

Like the Norwegian, Carrick is a dedicated club man and unlikely to rock the boat. Once again on Wednesday night, he declined the opportunity to place any blame on an underwhelming transfer window.

Since Everton stunned United with a stoppage-time equaliser 11 days ago (pictured), the Red Devils have lost the Manchester derby and been dumped out of the cup by Brighton

New No 2 goalkeeper Karl Darlow had an inglorious debut against the Seagulls, letting in three goals

United failed to land their top midfield transfer targets, and the most expensive one – £70million Carlos Baleba – arrived with an injury which means he won’t make his debut until October.

The new No 2 goalkeeper, Karl Darlow, was signed as a free agent and had an inglorious debut against Brighton, letting in three goals.

The forwards recruited last year, Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, have made a slow start to their second season at the club.

And next summer’s defensive rebuild cannot come soon enough, judging by the loss to Brighton. Two of United’s young prospects, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven, looked fragile in central defence, and the decision not to sign cover for Luke Shaw at left back appears increasingly flawed.

Shaw missed his third game in a row and Noussair Mazraoui, the latest player to deputise in his position, was struggling long before he was exposed for the winning goal scored by Maxim De Cuyper.

Carrick has been around United long enough to know not to press the panic button. He will have regained his composure by the time he faces the media again at Carrington on Friday.

Win at Fulham this weekend and he can go into the international break with room to breathe and time to fix the early-season problems without any additional pressure.

Lose again, and it will feel like we’re back in familiar territory.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel claims 99% of England fans don't discuss his Argentina mistakes - as he hands Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer recalls
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel claims that ’99.9 per cent’ of the England fans he has met since the World Cup have not even mentioned the crushing semi-final loss to Argentina in Atlanta.

Despite the fact that England went in to retreat after taking the lead against Lionel Messi & Co to lose 2-1, Tuchel says that supporters he meets only want to talk about the positives.

Tuchel was heavily criticised for defensive substitutions in the second half that night but said: ‘I know 99.9 per cent of the fans don't talk to me about substitutions, tactical tweaks or tactical details.

‘They speak about where they watched the Mexico game, and they speak about the second-half energy of the Croatia match.

‘They speak about how nerve-racking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

‘This is the feedback I get. This is what we created, and how it should be.’

Subsequently pressed on the matter, Tuchel admitted he had ‘some bad stuff between the Argentina game and France third place game’ but this is understood to have been a reference to media or social media comments.

Apart from that Tuchel feels he has the support of the country ahead of a Nations League campaign that begins with a home game against World Champions Spain a week today.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was the surprise name in Tuchel’s 27-man squad. The Real Madrid star hasn’t played for England since June 2025 but has been recalled after fellow right-backs Reece James, Djed Spence and Ben White all picked up injuries.

Cole Palmer, meanwhile, is also back after recovering form and fitness at Chelsea.

The England manager said: ‘Their quality is undisputed but they need to show it.’

Tuchel said in his opening England press conference two years ago that the former Liverpool player had to always concentrate on his defending.

Asked last night whether he offered enough defensively, Tuchel said: ‘He has to, he has to. It’s necessary.

‘My conviction is that he will but he has no choice.’ Tuchel said he initially hoped to choose a similar squad to his World Cup one only for injuries to force his hand.

As a result there are also call-ups for Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott along with Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

One player facing an almost impossible road back is Harry Maguire. The Manchester United defender Tweeted about his exclusion from the World Cup squad before it had even been announced last May while his mother said on social media she was ‘absolutely disgusted’ by the decision.

Asked whether the door was now closed on Maguire, Tuchel said: ‘I will not hold it against him for the rest of his life, because I'm not that type of person.

‘I can forget easily and quickly, but I didn't like it and it doesn't help.’

Sports.title: Michael Carrick comes out fighting: Under-fire Manchester United boss insists it is 'ridiculous' to question his Old Trafford future amid dismal start to the season
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick comes out fighting: Under-fire Manchester United boss insists it is 'ridiculous' to question his Old Trafford future amid dismal start to the season

Michael Carrick insisted the Manchester United job is still the right one for him as he hit back at the ‘ridiculous’ speculation over his future at Old Trafford.

The under-fire United boss came out fighting at Carrington on Friday after his team’s poor start to the season continued with back-to-back home defeats against Manchester City and Brighton.

Carrick took the blame for a dismal run of results but argued that United are not in the midst of ‘a catastrophe or disaster’, and that losing half of their six games this season ‘doesn’t mean the world caves in’.

When it was put to him that club owners can be influenced by external pressure and kneejerk reactions, Carrick dismissed any concerns over losing his job.

‘That's irrelevant for me,’ he said. ‘I know the club, I know the role. I understand where we need to be as a football club for the owners, and what they expect. For the supporters, as much as anything, and what they expect. I get all that.

‘But in terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, that's just totally not in my thinking. Not one part of it. Like, how long have I got. It's just ridiculous to think that way in the position that I'm in. That's just not on the radar.

‘We're living in a world of instant reaction, instant judgement, which is fine. It's how it is. But it's not in my world.’

Asked if United still feels like a great club at times of crisis, he added: ‘Yes, 100 per cent. I wouldn't want to be anywhere else, genuinely. It's the best place for me to be.

‘You've got to put things in a little bit (of perspective). It's not a catastrophe or a disaster. It's not the end of the world. We're not in a place where we've gone on an awful long run of horrific results, you know?

‘We've lost a couple of games recently and we feel like we've been in all the games that we've played, so it's not like we're having a real struggle all the time.

‘It's the beauty of being here at this football club. There's great times, there's things you can achieve and there's great feelings. And there's obviously the disappointments. Sometimes the smaller disappointments lead to being a little bit bigger. It's just part of coping and being at this great football club.

‘That's why I'm here. It's my responsibility, and I'm fine with that. It's not a blame game. We all search for things to look at and point somebody, or whatever reason it may be, and find a blame.

‘Blame me, no problem. I'll take the responsibility, whatever it is. But, for us, it’s not about blaming people. It's about finding solutions and being better.

‘It's two or three games that we haven't had certain results – and two or three games too many because I really hate losing. But that doesn't mean the world caves in.’

Carrick was on the front foot and it was typical of his approach that he challenged the question when asked if he needs to show more emotion. ‘I need to show more emotion?’ he shot back. ‘In what way? How? What do you want me to show?’

United were booed off the pitch by fans after giving up a two-goal lead in the 3-2 Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton on Wednesday night, but Carrick admitted that he was expecting a dip at some point.

‘It doesn't affect of how I think about what we need to do next,’ he said. ‘It doesn't knock us or put us off track or think about things we don't control.

‘I think we're always learning. When you're trying to build towards something, it's not always going to go to plan. History tells you that any team that's been successful goes through periods when you’ve got to work through it.

‘I was expecting at point at some stage that we'd go through it. It was going to come. We had such a good spell last season and going into this season, there was going to be a time when you don't get everything out of it what you wanted.

‘Winning games is always the answer. It's the answer to a lot of things. It can cover up a lot of things as well sometimes, by winning games and people don't see the whole picture, so it works both ways.’

Sports.title: The secrets of West Brom's rise revealed: A new recruitment strategy, James Morrison's extraordinary dedication behind the scenes, the academy conveyor belt and the boardroom rebuild
Sports.content:
Joint top of the Championship with a club legend at the helm and chasing a seventh win this century at the home of their greatest rivals. West Bromwich Albion are on the march again and while these are early days, the turbulence of last season is starting to fade from memory.

On Sunday, West Brom tackle Wolves in one of English football’s great fixtures and Baggies fans head for Molineux feeling positive.

Promising head coach James Morrison has guided Albion to 14 points from seven games, the finances look much healthier and supporters have a team starting to make them proud again.

Most importantly, chairman Shilen Patel and the Bilkul Football group appear to have found their feet, two-and-a-half years into their tenure. There should be no repeat of the chaos of last winter, when Eric Ramsay was sacked after only 44 days in charge.

Albion understand there will be trickier days ahead. Yet nearly two years after their impressive boss Carlos Corberan left for Valencia, they are feeling good about themselves once more. And in Morrison, they might just have found Corberan’s natural successor.

As they prepare for the season’s first Black Country derby, Daily Mail Sport looks at how West Brom are building for the future...

West Brom have made a fine start to the season and sit fourth on 14 points, the same total as league leaders West Ham

Club legend Morrison, who takes his team to rivals Wolves on Sunday, was rewarded with a two-year deal last April after keeping Albion up

A CLEAR PLAN

Even when West Brom were staring at relegation to League One, they already knew which way they would go this season. There were plans for both divisions but the focus was clear – invest in youth.

Finally clear of EFL financial restrictions, Albion paid fees totalling £15million for eight outfield players and of those, only 27-year-old midfielder Felix Horn Myhre was over the age of 23.

Midway through last season, Patel discussed the way forward with director of football Ian Pearce and technical director Dominic Price. The trio concluded that if Albion could stay up, it was the perfect chance to reset.

Karlan Grant had been costing the club £2.5m per season under the terms of his move from Huddersfield in 2020 but this summer, his contract finally expired. Other high earners Jed Wallace, Krystian Bielik and Alex Mowatt departed, along with Daryl Dike and Josh Maja.

Albion know that if summer buys Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Rabby Nzingoula or Kareem Tunde shine this season, they may not be able to keep hold of them. It would also mean selling at a profit – far better than watching a highly-paid player in his late-20s or early-30s drift out of contract.

If money is a player’s motivation, you might as well sign him when he’s young and hungry. The standard pay bracket in the second tier is £10-15,000 a week and West Brom are still striving to lower their wage bill since their parachute payments expired in 2023.

You want a better contract? Perform well and you’ll get one. How about Premier League wages? Attract the attention of those clubs by delivering for Albion. This is surely preferable to signing a wealthy journeyman who, naturally, will have at least one eye on his final ‘big’ contract.

Morrison does not scout the players, but Albion would never sign one he had vetoed. Similarly, his recommendations will be heeded.

Former Manchester United midfielder Toby Collyer was on a list of midfielders presented to Morrison as possible targets. Once Morrison insisted Collyer was the only one he wanted, Albion got the £3m deal done. In the case of Morgan, Nzingoula or Tunde, Morrison was handed the information and gave his approval.

West Brom do not pretend this is a revolutionary strategy. At least it is a strategy, though. Don’t forget that last January, West Brom hired Ramsay on the strength of his interview the previous June. Whatever supporters think of the current offering, at least they understand what the club are trying to achieve.

Jimmy-Jay Morgan, 20, joined the Baggies from Chelsea in the summer and already has five goals to his name in all competitions

Albion paid fees totalling £15million this summer for eight outfield players and of those, only 27-year-old midfielder Felix Horn Myhre (pictured) was over the age of 23

NO MORE 'MOZZA’

Morrison was an Albion hero long before he even thought of management. He played for the club from 2007 to 2019, making 341 appearances.

He immediately started coaching in Albion’s impressive academy and when Sam Allardyce was appointed in December 2020, he promoted Morrison to his own backroom team.

With Albion in freefall last February, Morrison stepped up where others might not have. Since then, he has overseen 21 matches in all competitions, winning nine and losing only four.

Even when Morrison was starting to pull West Brom clear of danger, few at the club genuinely believed he would be the long-term solution. He was still ‘Mozza’ rather than ‘Boss’ or ‘Gaffer’. Indeed, when club staff called him ‘Gaffer’ back then, it was usually in jest.

They would not do that anymore. Morrison was rewarded with a two-year deal last April after keeping Albion up and he made his mark instantly.

When all other football staff departed on holiday at the end of the season, Morrison was at the training ground every day for that first fortnight.

The 40-year-old could not rest until he had finalised his coaching team, now comprising Matt Gill, Gavin Strachan, Tony McMahon and Boaz Myhill, and mapped out exactly what pre-season would look like.

Until that was locked down, Morrison ignored those who urged him to take a break. That appetite for hard work is undimmed: after the 1-1 draw with QPR last Saturday, Morrison granted two days off. While his players and colleagues were recharging, Morrison spent a full day at the training ground on Monday, making plans for Molineux.

When all other football staff departed on holiday at the end of the season, Morrison was at the training ground every day for that first fortnight

Born in Darlington, County Durham and a product of the Middlesbrough academy, Morrison is a pleasing contrast to many modern bosses, with their buzzwords that come straight from a coaching manual.

He is quiet, a good listener, and gives simple messages to players. The basic framework is 4-4-2 but this structure can be tweaked game by game depending on the opponent.

There were some at Albion who believed Morrison may become their manager one day – but many more were unsure. Very few envisaged him managing other clubs after Albion. Perhaps, deep down, Morrison wondered the same.

Now, though, those same observers cannot imagine Morrison in any other role and if he, too, harboured those doubts, they have surely disappeared. The Albion boss certainly isn’t plain old ‘Mozza’ anymore.

ACADEMY BENEFITS

West Brom are close to agreeing a new deal with homegrown midfielder Harry Whitwell, whose contract expires at the end of the season. The 20-year-old has impressed this season and has interest from elsewhere, including Premier League clubs, but Albion officials are very optimistic that he will stay at the Hawthorns.

Even in the tough times, Albion continued to fund their academy and it has delivered. Tom Fellows was sold to Southampton for a possible £10m. Goalkeeper Alex Palmer joined Ipswich in a deal worth up to £4m.

Fans were not happy the club received only £6m when Dara O’Shea moved to Burnley in 2023 but at the time, Albion were probably six months from going into administration.

The respected Training Ground Guru platform recently ranked Albion’s academy – which retains Category One status – the 10th best in the country.

Morgan Rogers is often cited as the one who got away. The England forward is now one of the most expensive players of all time, having joined Chelsea from Aston Villa for £117m last summer. He cost Manchester City only £5m when they took him from Albion's academy aged 17 – yet once a wealthy Premier League club arrive on the scene, youth players are very hard to keep. It is doubtful Albion would have received any more had the matter gone to tribunal.

Under the stewardship of Richard Stevens, who has just completed seven years at the club, the academy is run with care and humility.

Though they lost key staff to Aston Villa during Christian Purslow’s time as CEO at Villa Park, Albion’s academy did not take significant damage. They are confident their methods will send more youngsters to the first team, with Whitwell the latest from the conveyor belt.

Albion have continued to fund their academy and it has delivered with Tom Fellows (right) sold to Southampton for a possible £10m

WHERE NEXT?

It has been a good start – but a start is all it is. It usually takes a little more than that to excite Albion supporters and not even a win over Wolves would have them all betting on promotion.

The most important factor now is that the key people share the same ideas. Mark Miles returned to the club as executive director last February following the departure of Andrew Nestor, who split opinion at the Hawthorns.

Miles has rebuilt the leadership team and the ownership group are prepared to allow their senior staff the space to do their jobs. Revenue was up eight per cent in the last accounts and losses down.

A long way to go, then, but West Brom are definitely heading in the right direction.

Sports.title: Man United's wantaway wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, flies to Barcelona for talks amid tug-of-war with Real Madrid after dropping quit bombshell
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s teenage star JJ Gabriel held talks with Barcelona on Friday as he prepares to choose between Europe’s top clubs over his next move.

Since Gabriel rocked United with a bombshell demand to quit Old Trafford, it has emerged that he is at the centre of a tug-of-war between Barca and their La Liga rivals Real Madrid.

It’s understood that the 15-year-old winger travelled to Spain via France on Thursday, raising the possibility that his representatives may have spoken to Paris Saint-Germain as well. Bayern Munich are also known to have been tracking his progress.

But Madrid have been leading the chase for Gabriel and are believed to have held talks with his camp over the past few weeks.

Barca made their pitch on Friday and have been keen on Gabriel for some time. The Catalan giants gave him a tour of their club facilities in August 2024 when he was introduced to superstar Lamine Yamal who signed a shirt and posed for a photo.

Manchester City and Chelsea are said to be monitoring the situation, but a move abroad feels more likely at this stage because Gabriel can join a European club two years earlier at 16 due to the fact he holds an Irish passport.

JJ Gabriel has flown to Barcelona for talks over a move to the LaLiga champions

Gabriel (pictured with Lamine Yamal in 2024) has told Man United he wants to leave the club

That would mean United only receiving around £300,000 in compensation, compared to a substantially higher fee if he joined a Premier League rival.

Gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football.

The youngster was set to sign a first-year scholarship at United at the age 16 – which would have automatically triggered a lucrative professional contract on his 17th birthday – and could even have made a first-team debut against Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night.

But he asked United to rip up his current deal which is due to expire at the end of the season. The club have so far refused to do so, but he could go to the Premier League or FIFA to force their hand and become a free agent.

He has not been seen at the club since he scored a hat-trick for the Under-21s on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah last week.

United boss Michael Carrick said at his press conference yesterday/on Friday that the youngster’s wellbeing remains paramount regardless of his future at Old Trafford.

‘I think I'd just repeat what I said the other day, really,’ said Carrick. ‘He's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important that we certainly don't play anything out here. I think the exposure and the scrutiny and everything, you’ve got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything.

‘So the situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's okay is the important thing.’

Sports.title: Chelsea thumped by Brentford as Jordan Henderson has nightmare return - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Chelsea thumped by Brentford as Jordan Henderson has nightmare return - 5 talking points

BRENTFORD 3-0 CHELSEA: Xabi Alonso's Blues are now three games without a win in the Premier League after being downed by their West London neighbours on Fridat evening

View 3 Images Chelsea are going through a mini-slump under Xabi Alonso (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea's Premier League struggles continued on Friday evening after being torn apart by West London rivals Brentford.

‌



Fans had to wait a while for their first goal of the game but Jaidon Anthony was on hand to nod the home side into a second-half lead.

‌



The Bees then took total control late on through last season's sensation Igor Thiago. Ex-Liverpool star Fabio Carvalho made sure of the points in stoppage time.

‌



It leaves Keith Andrews' men flying high in the Champions League places, while the Blues are now three league games without a win.

Here are all of the talking points from the Gtech Community Stadium:

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Brentford fans make feelings clear

It was a surprise to see England's Jordan Henderson seal a move to Chelsea this summer. And while Brentford were happy to facilitate his switch across West London, the same cannot be said of Bees fans.

Making his full debut for the Blues, he was loudly booed by the home supporters with every touch. And it ended up being a nightmare return, with his new employers slipping to a miserable defeat.

‌



In Henderson's defence, he was not the only one given a somewhat hostile reception. Argentina star Valentin Barco was also booed following his antics at this summer's World Cup.

View 3 Images Jordan Henderson made his first return to Brentford following his move to Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Schuster shines

Given how dangerous Chelsea have been going forwards, Brentford did an excellent job at keeping them at arms' length. A major factor behind that was Jannik Schuster.

‌



Before Friday evening's game, he had only started one Premier League game following his summer move from Red Bull Leipzig. But he looked more than at home.

He marshalled Danny Welbeck extremely well, while he also provided a crucial block to halt Morgan Rogers' goal-bound effort. The 20-year-old also notched an assist in what was an impressive display.

Anthony strikes first

Chelsea can't say they weren't warned on a few occasions before they went behind. Brentford were a serious threat from set pieces throughout the evening, while Anthony also threatened to give the Bees the lead, having seen a headed effort tipped over by Emi Martinez - albeit having been flagged offside.

‌



But Chelsea had no such let-off just after the hour mark. A corner was fired towards the far post and it was nodded back across goal by Schuster.

It left Anthony unmarked and he had the simple task of nodding home his first goal for the Bees.

View 3 Images Jaidon Anthony nods home his first Brentford goal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Chelsea's dismal defence

Given how sparkling the Blues' attack has been under Xabi Alonso so far this season, the Spanish coach still hasn't quite been able to fix an issue that has troubled them throughout the past year: their defence.

It's now 21 Premier League games without a clean sheet for the West Londoners, a truly dismal record. In fact, they've already conceded 12 goals in the league this season - no other side in the entire league have a leakier defence.

If Alonso wants to achieve anything at Stamford Bridge, he really needs to put some serious work into tightening Chelsea up at the back.

‌



Igor Thiago back in the goals

After a sensational campaign last term, Brazilian forward Igor Thiago has had somewhat of a nightmare this term. Ahead of taking on Chelsea, he was without a goal in the Premier League and that looked likely to continue on Friday.

He struggled throughout the evening, with little coming off. That was until the closing stages as he tapped home from Martinez's save from Kevin Schade's effort.

It was just the type of goal that he needed and he will certainly hope that his strike can kick-start his campaign.

Sports.title: England squad: Palmer and Trent back as snubbed star's partner takes aim at Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has announced his latest England squad as the Three Lions all prepare for an extended, revamped three-week international break across late September and early October

Thomas Tuchel has named his 26-man England squad for the upcoming international break. Chelsea's Cole Palmer and Real Madrid's Trent Alexander-Arnold have received recalls.

Palmer has impressed under Xabi Alonso this season, scoring four times and adding two assists in five appearances. He is back in the Three Lions camp after missing the World Cup. Another face returning to the England fold is Alexander-Arnold, despite a difficult start to the season at Real Madrid, where he has been in and out of the XI alongside Denzel Dumfries.

Elsewhere, Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha have been selected by Tuchel, who were included in the four-person warm-up group before the World Cup earlier this summer. Lewis Hall also makes it following an excellent start to the season at Newcastle United, while Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite has earned a place as a reward for a solid start to the campaign.

Sports.title: Jordan McCann QUITS boxing after KO defeat to 'UK's Hardest Man'
Sports.content:
Jordan McCann QUITS boxing after KO defeat to 'UK's Hardest Man'

The Manchester rapper has called time on his boxing career just days after suffering a brutal defeat to the 'UK's Hardest Man' - also known as Big Stacks

View Image Jordan McCann shows off his injuries just days after losing to big Stacks

Jordan McCann has officially QUIT boxing just days after losing to the 'UK's Hardest Man.'

‌



McCann and the 'UK's Hardest Man' - commonly known as Big Stacks - finally settled their rivalry months after the former had sucker-punched Stacks in the build-up to a Misfits event earlier this year.

‌



The pair clashed in Newcastle on Saturday night - with Stacks, real name Charlie Robert, using his size advantage early after repeatedly landing jabs on McCann. The Manchester rapper was struggling to see out of his right eye and when the fight was paused in the second round for it to be inspected, the doctor had no option but to wave off the contest, handing Big Stacks the win.

‌



On Friday afternoon, McCann took to social media to show off his battle scars following his clash with Big Stacks and revealed to his fans that he would not be fighting again. "A week after the fight now. I do not look too bad you know what I mean?" he began.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Conor Benn has world title shot shut down just days after Ryan Garcia loss READ MORE :

"But, I really had a good time doing the Misfits. I really appreciate it and I appreciate Mams (Taylor) and stuff. But yeah, I will not be doing that again. Not that I am scared or nothing.... but I still process like... it's good. It's a very good thing to get in and get out. Got a main event in my second fight, took over the show. That's always my plan, but it's just not for me. I have always been online with my music.

"It's just to be happy and do music and do whatever. Calling people names and targeting people and bullying people, it's not my way. It has never been my way my whole life. Just the whole process, the people you have to deal with... it's not for me. I am focused on my music now. I have had two fights - got some good money off it. And yes, I just want to say thanks to Misfits, thanks to everyone... but I am the worst boxer that ever lived. I am no good."

McCann's loss to Big Stacks marked his second defeat under the Misfits banner after he was beaten by Ibiza Final Boss on his debut earlier this year. Stacks had lost a comical 'body shot only' bout with Armz Korleone earlier this year before picking up his first Misfits win against McCann.

Article continues below

When asked who he wanted to fight next, he called out Martyn Ford, who is also known as the World's Strongest Man. "I'm the hardest man and I'm here to stay," he said. "Martyn Ford, he's a big donut; I want him next. He's big but he's a prick. I want to smash his head. I want to kick his head in."

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel flies in for transfer talks with Barcelona after Man Utd respond to request
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel flies in for transfer talks with Barcelona after Man Utd respond to request

Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel has been in the spotlight ever since his shock request to leave Old Trafford this week

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is keen to leave Old Trafford (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has reportedly arrived in Barcelona for talks. It comes just days after he stunned Old Trafford chiefs with his request to have his registration with the club cancelled, something United have rejected.

‌



The academy star could have been in line for his first-team debut at United on Wednesday night. The Red Devils had planned to include Gabriel in their squad to face Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup third round. It would have made the 15-year-old United’s youngest-ever first-team player.

‌



But that did not happen after his stunning request was made earlier this week. Concern grew over Gabriel after he deleted all pictures on his Instagram profile last week. The unusual behaviour came without any explanation, but his desire to leave may offer one.

‌



JJ Gabriel snubbed for England youth call-ups days after Man Utd star demanded to quit READ MORE :

Michael Carrick points blame for Man Utd struggles and responds to sack question READ MORE :

Now, Barcelona are set for talks over a potential deal. Fellow European giants Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich are also interested.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gabriel's camp submitted a formal request for United to deregister him this week, but it was denied. The club are still trying to convince him to stay at the club.

‌



However, that looks increasingly unlikely now that Gabriel and his entourage are in Spain. The player could hold talks with Real as well as Barca over a transfer next month.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel's time at Man United looks to soon be up

Although United have Gabriel under contract until the end of this season, there is a precedent for him to move abroad after he turns 16 on October 6 if he holds an EU passport, exploiting a FIFA loophole to sign for the La Liga giants.

‌



He could qualify for that through his father's Irish connections or his mother's Cypriot background and reports in Spain suggest he will obtain the relevant documentation to complete a move next week.

United could then be powerless to prevent it, although any move would still require FIFA approval. United can offer scholarship terms to Gabriel from his 16th birthday and although he now appears certain to leave, doing so should ensure they receive modest compensation.

‌



Red Devils head coach Michael Carrick was asked for an update on the situation at his press conference after the dismal Brighton defeat on Wednesday night.

The 45-year-old said: "I just think we've got to be really careful of the whole situation, you know.

"He's a young boy, he's 15, and for me, definitely, and from a club point of view, is looking after our younger players, their welfare, their well-being, their exposure, and I think we've got to be really, all of us, I think we've got to be really conscious of that, really, in this situation."

Article continues below

When Carrick was asked whether he gets involved with conversations over Gabriel's future, or leaves it to club chiefs, he responded: "No, as a club for sure, we're all involved in those conversations. I just think we've got to be very careful, you know, of that."

Sports.content:

Sports.title: Michael Carrick points blame for Man Utd struggles and responds to sack question
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick points blame for Man Utd struggles and responds to sack question

Manchester United have won just two of their opening six games in all competitions and there's pressure on Michael Carrick ahead of their clash with Fulham on Sunday

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is happy to take the flack (Image: MUTV)

Steadfast Michael Carrick has told fans to 'blame me' for Manchester United's dismal start to the season. The Red Devils have only mustered four points from their opening four Premier League games ahead of Sunday's trip to Fulham.

‌



Carrick's side were also dumped out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle in midweek. United threw away an early two-goal lead and lost 3-2 at home to Brighton, compounding their misery after a controversial defeat to rivals City in the Manchester derby four days prior.

‌



Facing questions over his position already, Carrick came out firing during his pre-match press conference and made it clear that he's happy to take the flack. "It's my responsibility, I'm fine with that," the United manager said.

‌



"It's not a blame game. We always search for things to look at and find the blame, sometimes it gets too much of wanting to find the blame. Blame me, it's no problem, but it's not about blaming people. It's about finding solutions. It's a whole collective thing.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It's about what you focus on really. I'm totally happy taking responsibility - no problem with that. I know where we want to get to and we want to get there fast.

Carrick also labelled the speculation over his future 'ridiculous', shooting down suggestions that he needs results quickly to avoid the sack. "I think that'll be a lot longer than one or two games of results," he continued.

"I understand, first of all, taking away all that, that's irrelevant for me. I know the club, I know the role, I know what's expected here in terms of playing to a certain standard, playing at a certain level, achieving certain things on the pitch, so I get all that.

‌



"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, I'm thinking one part of it, like how long have I got, it's ridiculous to think that way in a position that I'm in, that's just not on the radar.

‌



"I understand what we need to achieve and where we need to be as a football club for the owners, what they expect, for the supporters as much as anything, I get all that.

"It's two or three games that we haven't had certain results, and two or three games too many because I really hate losing, but that doesn't mean that the world caves in. In some minds it does, it can't for us, because we've got to perform."

Carrick also provided updates on Luke Shaw and Carlos Baleba, saying that both players have a 'chance' to feature at Craven Cottage. Baleba is yet to make his debut for the Red Devils since moving to Old Trafford in August for £70million because of an ankle injury.

"Not totally 100 per cent on either," Carrick explained. "It is really short term [with Shaw] but it is just working towards the game."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
